subsystems.name: Sleep-staging sensor array
subsystems.role: detects which sleep stage the wearer is in, second by second, without a gel-and-wire lab setup.
parts: dry EEG electrodes at forehead and behind the ear
analogue front end with motion artefact rejection

subsystems.name: Real-time controller
subsystems.role: classifies the current stage and decides exactly when a stimulus is allowed.

subsystems.name: Cue delivery
subsystems.role: replays sounds, words or odours tied to material learned during the day — the one part with solid lab evidence.

subsystems.name: Electrical stimulation path
subsystems.role: weak transcranial current applied to the scalp to bias cortical rhythms.

subsystems.name: Magnetic stimulation path
subsystems.role: the ambitious claim — pulsed magnetic fields to drive specific cortical patterns in a headband.

subsystems.name: Stimulus library and synchronisation
subsystems.role: pairs the daytime learning material with the cues that will be replayed at night.
parts: privacy controls for recorded brain data

buildSteps.title: Build the sensing band
buildSteps.detail: Dry, springy electrodes are pressed through hair on the forehead and mastoid; impedance and comfort are tested over multi-hour wear.

buildSteps.title: Validate sleep staging
buildSteps.detail: The classifier's stage calls are compared against simultaneous full polysomnography in a sleep lab, and disagreement rates are measured against how much the stimulus timing actually matters.

buildSteps.title: Pick the stimulation modality
buildSteps.detail: Audio and odour cues are cheap, safe and already work in labs; transcranial current is next; wearable magnetic stimulation is ruled in or out on acoustics, weight and power.

buildSteps.title: Pair cues with daytime learning
buildSteps.detail: Participants learn a task while a distinct sound is played; that sound becomes the retrieval key to be replayed later.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The controller waits for the target stage — slow-wave sleep for memory, REM for dream-content work — and fires a cue only when the pattern is stable and arousal risk is low.

buildSteps.title: Test against sham
buildSteps.detail: Every claimed effect — better recall, more lucid dreams — must survive blinded comparison with an identical headband that delivers nothing.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and shrink
buildSteps.detail: Electronics, battery and shielding are packed into a washable shell light enough to sleep in, with thermal and pressure safety margins.

buildSteps.title: Regulate
buildSteps.detail: A device that claims to alter memory or dreams is a medical device in most markets, needing clinical evidence and approval before sale.

buildSteps.title: Longer-run field study
buildSteps.detail: Months of home use, checked against objective tests, to see whether any gain persists or fades.

prerequisites.why: consumer sleep bands get stage calls roughly right but not reliably enough to time stimulation to a brain rhythm.

prerequisites.tech: Automatic sleep staging from few channels
prerequisites.why: accurate staging is the gate on every closed-loop claim.
replaying sounds or odours tied to daytime learning has been shown to shift memory in lab studies, but effects are modest and materials are specific.
magnetic coils need large pulse currents, cooling and heavy shielding, and click loudly — an unsolved fit for a headband worn during sleep.
sleep is known to consolidate what was already learned; evidence for acquiring genuinely new complex skills overnight is weak.

pathway.milestone: research rigs using polysomnography, cue replay and weak scalp current to nudge sleep rhythms and sometimes trigger lucid dreams
pathway.unlocks: proof that external stimulation can reach a sleeping brain at the right moment.

pathway.milestone: consumer headbands that stage sleep and play quiet closed-loop audio to deepen slow-wave sleep
pathway.unlocks: a wearable platform, though with a narrow and disputable benefit.

pathway.milestone: clinically validated memory-cueing for rehabilitation, for example after stroke or in early cognitive decline
pathway.unlocks: a real medical use for the loop, tested against sham.

pathway.milestone: the marketing claims in this tile — fast skill acquisition and controlled dreaming from a headband
pathway.unlocks: nothing, until wearable magnetic or electrical stimulation, brain-state decoding and a theory of how the stimulation produces a skill all exist together.
